mechaber/1:main: The order of prayer on the second night of Passover and counting the Omer. It has 10 seifim: On the second night after ma'ariv one begins to count the Omer; if he forgot at the beginning of the night he continues and may count the entire night. It is a mitzvah for each person to count for himself. One must count standing and recite a berachah first, and counts the days and weeks. How? On the first day one says "Today is one day (of the Omer)" until he reaches seven days, then he says "Today is seven days, which are one week (of the Omer)." On the eighth day he says "Today is eight days, which are one week and one day (of the Omer)," and likewise until fourteen days he says "Today is fourteen days, which are two weeks (of the Omer)," and in this manner he counts until 49 days.
mechaber/2:main: If they erred on an overcast day and blessed on counting the Omer, they return to count when it darkens. The meticulous do not count until the emergence of stars, and so it is proper to act.
mechaber/3:main: One who prays with the congregation while still day counts with them without a berachah; if he remembers at night he blesses and counts. {Rama: And even if he answered amen to the congregation's berachah, if his intent was not to fulfill, he returns and blesses and counts at night (Beit Yosef in the name of Rashba}.}
mechaber/4:main: If a friend asks him during twilight how many days of the count are on this night, he tells him "yesterday were such-and-such," for if he tells him "today is such-and-such" he cannot return and count with a berachah; but before twilight, since it is not time for counting, it does not matter. {Rama: And when the time arrives it is forbidden to eat until he counts; even if he began eating he stops and counts. However, if he began eating before the time arrived he need not interrupt but finishes his meal and counts afterward (this is his own view for those who hold counting in our time is d'oraisa}.}
mechaber/5:main: If he does not know the reckoning and opened with intent to conclude as he will hear from his friend, and was silent until he heard from his friend and concluded like him, he has fulfilled.
mechaber/6:main: If he opened and said "Baruch Atah... Elokeinu Melech ha'olam" intending to say "today is four," thinking they are four, and remembered and concluded with "five" and they are five; or conversely they are four and he opened intending to say four and erred and concluded with five — he does not return and bless again.
mechaber/7:main: If he forgot and did not bless all night, he counts by day without a berachah.
mechaber/8:main: If he forgot to bless on one of the days, whether the first day or other days, he counts on the remaining days without a berachah; but if he is uncertain whether he skipped one day and did not count, he counts on the remaining days with a berachah.
mechaber/9:main: On Shabbat night and Yom Tov night one blesses and counts after kiddush in the synagogue; at Motzei Shabbat and Motzei Yom Tov, before havdalah after Kaddish Titkabel; and when the last Yom Tov of Passover falls on Motzei Shabbat, when one says kiddush and havdalah together, one should count before blessing on the cup in the synagogue. {Rama: And if he has no wine and must make kiddush he recites the acronym — see above siman 296.}
mechaber/10:main: It is forbidden to eat chadash even in our time, whether bread, roasted grain, or fresh grain, until the beginning of the night of the 18th of Nisan; in Eretz Yisrael until the beginning of the night of the 17th of Nisan.
baer-heitev/1:א: (א) At night. They say the ma'arivim belonging to the second night even if the first day falls on Shabbat — for other festivals, if the first day falls on Shabbat they say on the second night the ma'arivim of the first day and the second is postponed; nevertheless on the second day of Passover they always say the ma'arivim belonging to that day because of prioritizing the omer count, and so is custom.
baer-heitev/1:ב: (ב) To count. See Magen Avraham and Kaf HaChayyim — women are exempt from counting, for it is a positive time-bound mitzvah — Rambam; however they have already made it obligatory upon them. Magen Avraham.
baer-heitev/1:ג: (ג) On. If he wishes he hears the berachah from the shaliach tzibbur and counts for himself, as it is written "you shall count" — the count shall be for each one — see Magen Avraham and Kaf HaChayyim; if he transgressed and heard the count from another he has fulfilled if listener and reciter intended — Peri Chadash, and see Yad Aharon on Beit Yosef's hagahah. It is simple one may count in any language, specifically one he understands; if he does not understand Holy Tongue and counted in Holy Tongue he did not fulfill, for he does not know what he says and this is not counting. Magen Avraham.
baer-heitev/1:ד: (ד) Standing. For it is written "when you rise" — do not read "when grain rises" but "when you rise"; b'dieved if he counted seated he fulfilled. Rambam.
baer-heitev/1:ה: (ה) And to bless. That we bless on this count and not on counting of niddah — see Radbaz part 1 siman 27 and see Kaf HaChayyim; that we do not bless shehecheyanu on counting because there is no joy and pleasure. Acharonim — see Kaf HaChayyim.
baer-heitev/1:ו: (ו) And the weeks. If he counted days alone and did not count weeks, or counted weeks alone and not days — he must return and count with berachah — Peri Chadash and so Maharshal Levi O.C. siman 5; but Kesef Mishnah, Magen Avraham, and Kaf HaChayyim agreed b'dieved he fulfilled; therefore it appears he counts without berachah, for berachot are not me'akev. Keset HaSofer wrote in Maharshal's name: if he counted in acronym e.g. "today 4 days" or said "8 days which are one week and one day" he fulfilled — Yoreh De'ah; Peri Chadash wrote he did not fulfill Yoreh De'ah; if he said "forty lacking one of the omer" he fulfilled — Mahari Mulcho, Yad Aharon.
baer-heitev/1:ז: (ז) Today. He should not say "that today" is last. Kaf HaChayyim wrote one who says "that today" was not mistaken — see there.
baer-heitev/1:ח: (ח) In the Omer. So too Taz and the Ari's text "la'omer," and so Shelah.
baer-heitev/1:ט: (ט) One. He should not say "one" in feminine, for "week" is masculine. He always puts the smaller number first, e.g. one and twenty days; until ten he says "days," from eleven upward says "day" — elegance in Holy Tongue; custom to say Psalm "Elohim yichaneinu" after counting — see Kaf HaChayyim.
baer-heitev/1:י: (י) 49. See what Rosh wrote in chapter Acharonim — some question: since the verse says count fifty days, Scripture's way at a round sum is to count in tens and not notice the lacking one, etc. — see there. Therefore question what the gemara wants in Kiddushin 38a: "Bnei Yisrael ate man forty years" — forty years lack thirty days — see there. Per Rosh there is no difficulty — such is Scripture's way; see Yad Aharon.
baer-heitev/2:א: (א) Returning. Meaning without berachah — Keset HaSofer.
baer-heitev/2:ב: (ב) Stars. If he erred and counted twilight he fulfilled — Magen Avraham. Some poskim hold even l'chatchila one counts in safeik of darkness — see Beit Yosef, Bach, Taz.
baer-heitev/3:א: (א) While still day. See Taz, Magen Avraham, Kaf HaChayyim; it appears permitted to count after stars emerge even if he has not prayed ma'ariv, even on Motzei Shabbat — Magen Avraham see there.
baer-heitev/3:ב: (ב) Not. Meaning in berachah; but in counting he is in any case obligated to count himself as seif 3 wrote. Magen Avraham wrote: specifically when his intent was not to fulfill; from silence it implies not to bless again from safeik — see there; however Taz in sk 6 is not so — see Kaf HaChayyim sk 15.
baer-heitev/4:א: (א) Today. If he said such-and-such and did not say "today" — we have no concern. Taz and Magen Avraham.
baer-heitev/4:ב: (ב) With berachah. Even though he did not say "ba'omer" he fulfilled b'dieved. Magen Avraham.
baer-heitev/4:ג: (ג) Time. Requires study — should half hour before time also be forbidden as siman 232? It appears where custom is the sun calls to count, one need not be stringent before time as siman 232 — Magen Avraham, see Kaf HaChayyim.
baer-heitev/5:_: Fulfilled. Implies b'dieved — Taz — but l'chatchila he should not bless until he has clarity how many days of sefirah.
baer-heitev/6:_: And bless. So Acharonim agreed — only counts again without berachah — see Kaf HaChayyim, Magen Avraham.
baer-heitev/8:_: Without. Specifically when he skipped an entire day — then no "temimot"; but if he forgot at night and counted by day, he may count coming days with berachah — Levush, Or Torah, and so is custom; what Baer Heitev wrote earlier in Taz's name was imprecise — see there. Shelah: where a group prays ma'ariv on time, fit to join them on counting days, for mitzvah draws mitzvah — Shema in time and counting in congregation.
baer-heitev/9:א: (א) Kiddush. Because entry of Shabbat pleases us more; but at home he counts before kiddush, for forbidden to eat before counting — Acharonim.
baer-heitev/9:ג: (ג) Of Passover. But the second day of Passover there is no kiddush at all in the synagogue as siman 487; Taz wrote it appears on the last Yom Tov night one always counts before kiddush of the last Yom Tov, for better to draw sanctity of the seventh day which is from Torah, and sanctity of the last Yom Tov is rabbinic — end quote; Kaf HaChayyim wrote this is against the Rav's implication that one always counts after kiddush unless Motzei Shabbat, and so is custom.
baer-heitev/10:_: Chadash. Magen Avraham wrote the world relies on what Rama wrote that chadash in ch"l is rabbinic and they did not decree now in ch"l since we do not rely on Eretz Yisrael — end quote; nevertheless a careful person should be stringent where possible — see Magen Avraham, Kaf HaChayyim, Beit Din siman 293 in Shach.
beer-hagolah/1:ד: (ד) At the end of the day, the snails from the groves evaporate, and
beer-hagolah/1:ה: (ה) Statement of Abaye there 15; Rif and Rosh wrote at the end of Pesachim
beer-hagolah/1:ו: (ו) Rosh in responsum, and Tur likewise
beer-hagolah/3:_: Dr. David is lost in the name of the Vitri cycle and the name of the taste
beer-hagolah/4:_: There: Rambam's wording that if one counted without blessing he fulfilled
beer-hagolah/5:_: A column called my fierce father
beer-hagolah/6:_: Beit Yosef per what Ran wrote: most commentators agree counting the omer nowadays is d'rabbanan, unlike Tur in the name of Abba ha-Ezri
beer-hagolah/7:_: A column called the Rashi and the rest of the world cease to know R
beer-hagolah/8:א: In the name of Halakhot Gedolot, and Tosafot likewise in his name; Menachot 66 as well
beer-hagolah/9:ד: (ד) The name of the Dish after the most significant difference we can
beer-hagolah/10:_: M.M.M. Darabina presents a warning sign:
machatzit-hashekel/1:א: (א) Even if, etc. — belonging to the seventh:
machatzit-hashekel/1:ב: (ב) And ma'ariv of the last day is postponed. End Sukkah 55a lists psalms of chol hamoed Sukkot; on sixth day they said Psalm 82; when one day of chol hamoed fell on Shabbat the special Shabbat song was postponed — e.g. if second chol hamoed was Shabbat, sixth day's song postponed and on third day they said second day's song, etc., until sixth day they said fifth day's; always the last "they totter" of sixth day is postponed — unlike Pozna custom.
machatzit-hashekel/4:א: (א) (ס"ק ד) And weeks, etc. — we hold rabbinic. Rama seif 4: if he began eating he stops — if rabbinic need not stop, as siman 235:2 — Kaf HaChayyim: since some hold d'oraisa, no loss in stopping briefly to count — satisfy those who hold d'oraisa.
machatzit-hashekel/4:ב: (ב) If he counted weeks alone he also fulfilled — Tur in Ravyah: may count so l'chatchila — until seven days count days; day seven say one week; day eight say one week and one day; not "eight days which are one week and one day" — not our practice; b'dieved rely on Ravyah.
machatzit-hashekel/5:א: (א) (ס"ק ה) Today — he should not say "that today." Kaf HaChayyim: even one who says "that today" is not mistaken — see there.
machatzit-hashekel/5:ב: (ב) Masculine language — therefore say one week not one (feminine); two weeks not two; three four five six seven end with heh; eight has heh for both genders — only vowel differs.
machatzit-hashekel/5:ג: (ג) Bach wrote in Even HaEzer 126 sk 9 in Levush's name: masculine nun kamatz, feminine segol; Taz in Taharot ch. 5 opposite for feminine kamatz like "ro'eh hi."
machatzit-hashekel/5:ה: (ה) Bach also: until ten say "days," from eleven say "day."
machatzit-hashekel/5:ו: (ו) Kaf HaChayyim here in Shelah's name: elegance in Holy Tongue; b'dieved not me'akev — see Even HaEzer. If he says ba'omer or la'omer — dispute; practice according to each authority.
machatzit-hashekel/5:ז: (ז) Yoma 55: High Priest counting sprinklings on Yom Kippur — R. Meir: one one, two two; R. Yehuda: one one, one two, one three; they do not argue — each locale per custom; Rashi: in R. Meir's place smaller number first, in R. Yehuda's larger first.
machatzit-hashekel/6:_: (ס"ק ו) Until, etc. — he fulfilled; some l'chatchila count twilight for completeness — we do not hold so; b'dieved rely on them.
machatzit-hashekel/7:א: (א) (ס"ק ז) One who prays, etc. — so Abudraham from whom Shulchan Aruch: ma'ariv with congregation while still day counts without berachah, saying: if I remember at night I will return and bless — not berachah levatalah; if I forget I already counted days and weeks for the mitzvah; Rambam: counted without blessing — fulfilled; Beit Yosef: nevertheless repair ruined — question why Rabbis wrote; Abudraham agrees with Rambam — not proper to do so.
machatzit-hashekel/7:ב: (ב) Beit Yosef implies he holds as corrected — question, for Abudraham agrees with Rambam.
machatzit-hashekel/7:ג: (ג) I do not intend to fulfill — stam he did not fulfill; Magen Avraham truth: even if Rabbis hold no intent needed, all agree if explicitly intent not to fulfill he did not fulfill; Rabbis in 489 hold mitzvot need intent; Beit Yosef 475.
machatzit-hashekel/7:ד: (ד) Twilight after ma'ariv — since night for Shabbat, so for counting — Kaf HaChayyim in Pesakkei Tosafot Menachot: even on chol if prayed ma'ariv may count; congregation relies on Magen Avraham, Rashba, Abudraham — not Taz who deals with twilight; we do not hold like Pesakkei Tosafot.
machatzit-hashekel/8:_: (ס"ק ח) His intent, etc. — requires intent; Magen Avraham brought Radbaz: rabbinic mitzvah needs no intent, and most hold counting rabbinic — nevertheless Shulchan Aruch stam requires intent — not like Radbaz; even rabbinic mitzvah needs intent.
machatzit-hashekel/10:_: (ס"ק י) He did not intend, etc. — all the more Radbaz sk 8 not like Taz; per Kaf HaChayyim sk 7 in Pesakkei Tosafot: after ma'ariv even still day one fulfills — likewise if prayed ma'ariv though still day, be careful not to tell friend how many days.
magen-avraham/1:א: (א) Even if the first day falls on Shabbat they say on the second night the ma'arivim of the second because of prioritizing the omer (Levush) — implies if seventh day of Passover falls on Shabbat they say on the last day ma'arivim of the seventh — see siman 642: in Pozna they do not practice so, but gemara end Sukkah implies the last is always postponed — see there. They begin to count. Kesef Mishnah ch. 6 Sukkah questioned how we bless on counting on second Yom Tov without concern for Yom Tov degradation, as we do not bless on sukkah on Shemini Atzeret — answered: there one says on the cup "this Yom Tov day" and blessing on sukkah would contradict; not so here. Or since we are expert in fixing the month, by law no need to sit in sukkah on Shemini Atzeret therefore no berachah; here by law one must count today therefore we bless — end quote. Women exempt — positive time-bound (Rambam; Zohar Tzav 119); however already made obligatory. Magen Avraham.
magen-avraham/1:ב: (ב) To count for himself. If he wishes to hear berachah from shaliach tzibbur and count for himself — all berachot even if expert one fulfills through shaliach tzibbur except Birkat Hamazon and Shema and prayer (Rashba responsa 126); here too he must count himself, as gemara "you shall count" — count for each one, as they said regarding lulav "you shall take" — taking for each one. Beit Yosef in Rashba's name: one fulfills through shaliach tzibbur's count — requires study; perhaps since we hold shome'a ke'oneh it is as if he counted himself. Simple one may count in any language he understands; if he does not understand Holy Tongue and counted in Holy Tongue he did not fulfill, for he does not know what he says — not counting.
magen-avraham/1:ג: (ג) Standing. If he counted seated he fulfilled (Rambam).
magen-avraham/1:ד: (ד) And weeks. It appears if he counted days alone and not weeks he need not return, as gemara for those who hold counting rabbinic; Beit Yosef in most poskim we hold counting today rabbinic; if he counted weeks alone he also fulfilled as Tur wrote.
magen-avraham/1:ה: (ה) Today. He should not say "that today," for it implies giving reason for what was counted above; rather "today day..." Weeks and days are masculine, as written "seven weeks." Always put smaller number first — see Even HaEzer siman 126; however Yoma 55a: all per local custom; in our land even in secular tongue we mention smaller number first. Some say Psalm Elohim yichaneinu after counting.
magen-avraham/2:_: Until stars. If he erred and counted twilight he fulfilled.
magen-avraham/3:א: (א) One who prays with congregation, etc. Rashba siman 235: one who said he counts with congregation while still day relies on nonsense of our Rabbi — all who count while still day did nothing; rather he testifies falsely; if he fears forgetting and relies on this count like Shema of ma'ariv — he already fulfilled sefirah and when he returns to bless it is berachah levatalah — end quote; so Abudraham concluded. But Rambam: counted and did not bless — fulfilled; Beit Yosef: nevertheless his repair ruined — perhaps he forgot first time and forbidden to bless again; why did Rabbis write this? It appears per his view mitzvot need intent — he intends: if I remember at night I do not intend to fulfill in this count, as Rama wrote intent not to fulfill; Hagah Maimoni: some permit counting twilight after ma'ariv; Bach wrote we do not hold so. It appears permitted to count after stars even before ma'ariv, even Motzei Shabbat — night is for all matters, even kiddush and havdalah before prayer; one fulfills Birkat Hamazon as siman 271, 293, 267; Sefer Chanukat HaBayit wondered why custom counts before havdalah while still Shabbat — no concern, Shabbat has passed, only melacha prohibitions until havdalah.
magen-avraham/3:ב: (ב) Intent not to fulfill. Question: even stam he did not fulfill, for he needs intent to fulfill as siman 60:4; perhaps since forbidden berachah levatalah, if stam forbidden to bless again since some hold mitzvot need no intent.
magen-avraham/4:א: (א) Today such-and-such. If he said such-and-such without "today" — we have no concern (Taz).
magen-avraham/4:ב: (ב) Cannot return to count. Even though he did not say ba'omer he fulfilled b'dieved; even though he did not intend to fulfill as sk 3.
magen-avraham/4:ג: (ג) And when time arrives. Requires study — should half hour before also be forbidden as siman 232 and 235? Perhaps Rashi Lublin did not eat until after counting because they leave synagogue half hour before night and he holds eating forbidden; see Mateh Moshe, Shelah; Rama's view: since time to count all night and next day we are not so stringent; nevertheless question the source; perhaps where sun calls to count one need not be stringent before time as siman 232 — perhaps Rama deals with that.
magen-avraham/6:_: (ו) And erred and concluded with five. Bach ruled he returns and blesses, for he spoke falsely; so many poskim siman 209, Levush — see there; however it appears he does not return and bless, only counts again, for in one berachah he fulfilled afterward unless he paused greatly; if he remembered within twenty-four hours and said four he fulfilled even if he did not know initially they are four, and all the more if he knew they are four but erred in speech and remembered within twenty-four hours — siman 209, 487.
magen-avraham/7:_: (ז) Without berachah. Because it is written "temimot."
magen-avraham/9:א: (א) After kiddush. We advance Shabbat as much as possible; at home he counts before kiddush, and forbidden to eat before counting as sk 4.
magen-avraham/9:ב: (ב) Before havdalah. Taking the day out afterward as much as possible.
magen-avraham/9:ג: (ג) One should count, etc. So Shabbat not be a burden.
magen-avraham/10:_: Forbidden to eat chadash. Avi Ezri 293: Rama permitted chadash; Shelah: not applicable in Poland where most grain is sown after Passover; precise for barley and oats; wheat and spelt mostly Cheshvan — no chadash — see Shach on beer from chadash; Rama responsa: even careful about chadash need not worry absorbed taste, for all chadash today is rabbinic safeik; even if certain prohibition nullified in majority d'oraisa, all the more chadash which is only general stringency — Maharai: do not derive from majority to forbid, we follow majority of old grain; therefore little concern for absorbed taste. Nullified in majority d'oraisa — chadash reason nullified in majority d'oraisa only min b'mino; meat cooking is not min b'mino — needs sixty d'oraisa — Avi Ezri 98. Majority of grain — when safeik which grain; if clear from new grain, forbidden even absorbed taste. World relies on Rama chadash ch"l rabbinic (Likutei Maharil); no decree now in ch"l; Tanya 491 Or Zaru'a: rabbinic, hold like Tanna Kamma; stam mishnah Orlah like R. Eliezer but stam and dispute; repeated Tanna Kamma in Kiddushin — stam as Beitzah beginning, later stam preferable — Tosafot Chullin 43; no Mishnah order but rule hold like Tanna Kamma (general rules 32 R. Yom Tov; Merutzach ch. 9 two orders have order — Taz Kiddushin, ch. 9 Sotah, ch. 7 Terumot; Tosafot Yevamot 42, end Shabbat prove no order in two orders). Rosh: R. Akiva argues — not difficult; Tanna Kamma holds moshvotechem wherever you dwell, grain from Eretz Yisrael to ch"l as Yerushalmi; R. Yosef: even Tanna Kamma chadash rabbinic, precise near Eretz Yisrael like terumah — Tosafot; settle custom, Taz too; careful person stringent where possible.
mishnah-berurah/1:א: (א) On the second night — Acharonim wrote they say Maariv belonging to day 2 even if second night falls on Motzei Shabbat; and although on other festivals if first day falls on Shabbat they say on second night Maariv of day 1 — here is different for Maariv is matter of counting
mishnah-berurah/1:ב: (ב) (b) After the fall of Arabic, and before we, we will be able to do more of what is written:
mishnah-berurah/1:ג: (ג) (c) It begins to count and so on - and women and slaves are exempt from this eviction that the time of Gramma and the book of the M.A., who has already been raised, is obligated, and as such, our countries are not female drivers at all to count and write in an entire table book that is certainly not the meaning of the word:
mishnah-berurah/1:ד: (ד) (d) Go and writer, and so on, if not passed through the night, we will not issue any of the written notes:
mishnah-berurah/1:ה: (ה) To count for himself — as written "and you shall count for yourselves" — mitzvah applies to each individual; it is implied from this in counting unlike other mitzvot dependent on speech regarding kiddush and havdalah etc. — if he heard another and intended to fulfill he fulfills because one who hears is as one who speaks; here Torah revealed he does not fulfill however much he did not count himself; but some Acharonim wrote Torah's intent is only it should not be said this mitzvah stands for court alone like Shemitta and Yovel where it says "and you shall count for yourself" — refers to congregation; but in truth if he heard from another who counted and intended to fulfill and also other intended to fulfill him — he fulfilled as everywhere we rule one who hears is as one who speaks; all this in counting; but in blessing they bless on counting — all agree possible to fulfill through another even if expert as in all blessings; nevertheless custom in all Israel each blesses and counts for himself and does not rely on prayer leader. Acharonim wrote counting is permitted in any language provided he understands that language; if he does not understand even if he counted in holy tongue he did not fulfill — since he did not know what he said it is not counting
mishnah-berurah/1:ו: (ו) (b) We have to count the standing, and we need to stand up from the time the blessing begins. And even if he was told, he said
mishnah-berurah/1:ז: (ז) And he counts days and weeks — as written "you shall count fifty days" and "seven weeks you shall count for yourself"; if he counted days alone and did not mention weeks — some say he fulfilled b'dieved and some say he must return and count days and weeks properly and therefore returns and counts without blessing [and if he forgot to return and count he counts remaining days with blessing]; if he counted weeks and not days such as on seventh day he said today one week and did not mention days at all — all agree he did not fulfill
mishnah-berurah/1:ח: (ח) In the omer — and most poskim nusach "to the omer"; however essence of this is only l'chatchila to clarify he counts from day they offered omer onward; if he only said today such-and-such he also fulfilled
mishnah-berurah/1:ט: (ט) (T) and on the day that a mini will say and so on - and if he did not say, it was eight days, and he did not finish that they were one week, and so on, he mentioned weeks yesterday on the seventh day, and if he did not say, but one week and one day in the Judenya has already mentioned the days that have passed each day. They say one week and not one. They say two weeks and not two minutes of male tongue. Up to 10 days, and who says day. It is important to say that the penile is such as one and twenty days and all of these things Not to delay but to the tongue:
mishnah-berurah/1:י: (י) And in this manner etc. — custom to say after counting "may it be His will" etc. to build Temple etc. — meaning then we fulfill mitzvah of bringing omer; some also practice saying Psalm "May Heaven grant us grace" etc.
mishnah-berurah/1:כ: (כ) (a) This and so on - the last of them, Dham said in another language, such as on the day of the High Court, forty, one missing man came out:
mishnah-berurah/2:א: (יב) They return etc. — Rashba's words responsum 254; explained there congregation also prayed Maariv before; regarding Maariv they should not return and pray because of congregation trouble (as above beginning siman 483 seif 14) — only regarding counting we are not concerned for their trouble lest he say for example ten days when only nine for that day is ninth not tenth until stars — end there
mishnah-berurah/2:ב: (ב) (c) count when you are dark, and in the blessed way:
mishnah-berurah/2:ג: (יד) And the punctilious — meaning by law it was possible to be lenient to count from darkening even before stars since twilight is rabbinic uncertainty and we follow leniency in rabbinic uncertainty in counting nowadays d'rabbanan for most poskim; nevertheless not proper to place oneself in uncertainty l'chatchila — therefore punctilious wait until stars which is certainly night
mishnah-berurah/2:ד: (טו) And so is proper — meaning l'chatchila; nevertheless b'dieved if he blessed in twilight he fulfilled as above; Avodat Yom Tov questions and sides proper he return and count at stars without blessing
mishnah-berurah/3:א: (טז) While still day — some Acharonim explained meaning twilight which is rabbinic uncertainty and they fulfill counting then for poskim who hold counting nowadays d'rabbanan; he wishes to be punctilious and count from stars as above; Mechaber says he counts with them lest he forget afterward and think in his mind if I remember at night to count I do not wish to fulfill with this counting — as in gloss below; therefore when time arrives afterward he blesses and counts; see Biur Halacha
mishnah-berurah/3:ב: (ב) (a) Not to go out, and if you wait for not to leave, but at the end of the day, it is possible for a blessing to be mentioned there:
mishnah-berurah/3:ג: (ג) He said, “He will bless you and count at night, and even if he has already received a Shabbat and also prayed with the Holy One, he will bless and count at night, for he did not want to leave what he said to them. In the last writings, if the stars came out, they were allowed to count not yet to pray from the cities, and even in the night-made prison, it is for all my gods and even for the temple and to distinguish it from the beginning of darkness, but that it is forbidden to complete until it is distinguished:
mishnah-berurah/4:א: (יט) Twilight etc. — he specified twilight because b'dieved if he blessed in twilight he fulfilled as above; and all the more if asked him after stars he must be careful not to answer today such-and-such
mishnah-berurah/4:ב: (ב) This is how it is, and so on, it is the same as it is. And if he did not say to him today, he would say so to him:
mishnah-berurah/4:ג: (כא) He cannot etc. — although he did not say "in the omer" he fulfilled b'dieved as above s.k. 8
mishnah-berurah/4:ד: (כב) To return and count with blessing — since he already fulfilled counting per those who say mitzvot do not require intent; although we rule they require intent and this one did not intend to fulfill this mitzvah — for blessing one must be stringent and be concerned for that view and not bless on counting he will count afterward; there is further advice to explicitly intend not to fulfill with this counting. Acharonim wrote deals if asked him before reaching weeks; if asked at hour reaching weeks even if said today such-and-such it is nothing if he did not mention weeks — must return and count with blessing
mishnah-berurah/4:ה: (ה) And when it comes to time, R.C. came to the stars and even if they were already praying, and the darkness of D.C. is forbidden from the dark and darkness. And the last paragraphs of May have been discussed above in the letter of Ral to make it more than half an hour earlier, “We have to make it worse not to eat from half an hour next to the AD and on [even if it is already preceded and prayed] but instead of the custom that the sun calls to count a count, there is no worsening for its time:
mishnah-berurah/4:ו: (ו) (Ps) To eat, and "the rest of the angels and the curses of the earth."
mishnah-berurah/4:ז: (כה) He stops and counts — per those who hold counting nowadays d'oraisa as in gloss; if so for us who hold d'rabbanan he does not stop — as above siman 232 regarding Minchah; some Acharonim wrote therefore Rama here in our matter was concerned to be stringent like that view since it is matter without any trouble to interrupt briefly and count
mishnah-berurah/4:ח: (ח) (b) Before the time has come – and by what we have written above, a half hour near the time begins, the prohibition will belong to Dana Darm when you start eating more than half an hour before time:
mishnah-berurah/4:ט: (ט) A. To stop, even to the D.C., there is still more to count:
mishnah-berurah/5:ב: (כט) And concluded like it he fulfilled — meaning even in blessing if he opened blessing with this intent and concluded; there is conclusion and opening; nevertheless l'chatchila he should not bless unless he knows from start which day it is — forbidden to interrupt even in silence between blessing and mitzvah more than kedei dibbur
mishnah-berurah/6:ב: (ב) (No) and he was wrong and wrong, and so on
mishnah-berurah/6:ג: (לב) He does not return and bless — Acharonim wondered on this law; granted initially concluding with five when it is five is fine he counted properly although at time of blessing he thought four — nothing since even without blessing at all he fulfilled; but in latter case what helps us that at time of blessing he knew which day — nevertheless in his mouth he counted wrong day; they agreed in this he must count anew and bless for first blessing was in vain since he concluded after it different day unless he remembered within kedei dibbur of his counting then he returns and counts properly and blessing counts; know further although Shulchan Aruch deals when at time of blessing he knew day of counting and blessed intending to count properly but afterward erred and concluded improperly; several Acharonim agreed even if at time of blessing his mind was also on different day and he erred in counting — nevertheless if within kedei dibbur he remembered he erred he immediately concludes properly and fulfills thus; further they wrote if he erred and said today day four of omer and within twenty-four he remembered it is day five — suffices he conclude fifth in omer and fulfills thus even if he did not say today day five since still within kedei dibbur
mishnah-berurah/7:א: (א) (g) will be counted on a day – as a lot of judgments of the A.D.:
mishnah-berurah/7:ב: (ב) (d) Without a blessing, it is enough to feel the opinion of the Phosicians, but at night, and when you walk in the day, it is to abolish who is from here and bring a writer every night in a welcome and not to go to a single day that is no longer known as anemia:
mishnah-berurah/8:א: (א) (a) Forget to bless you and so on. "If he was told that yesterday he was wrong with Lenin and another book of count as he did not say at all:
mishnah-berurah/8:ב: (לו) He counts on other days — per many poskim days do not impede each other; each day and day is mitzvah by itself
mishnah-berurah/8:ג: (ג) (לז) Without berachah — to be concerned for the view that we require seven complete weeks, and this is lacking one day; correct in this that he hear the berachah from the shaliach tzibbur or one of those who bless and answer amen with intention to fulfill, and afterward he counts [Eshel Avraham and Peri Chadash].
mishnah-berurah/8:ד: (wet / having liquid) He counts remaining days with blessing — there is double doubt: perhaps he did not skip at all; and if skipped perhaps halacha follows those poskim each day is mitzvah by itself; likewise in any matter whose law is to return and count without blessing from doubt — if he did not return and count he counts remaining nights with blessing [Acharonim]; therefore if erred in days and not weeks or erred in weeks and not days — law is return and count without blessing as above s.k. 7; if he did not return and count nevertheless he counts remaining days with blessing; see Biur Halacha
mishnah-berurah/9:א: (לט) After kiddush in synagogue — all we can advance sanctity of day we advance; if he counts at home he counts before kiddush for forbidden to eat before counting as above
mishnah-berurah/9:ב: (ב) (b) First of all, Dufoy Yumma is because of all this is possible:
mishnah-berurah/9:ג: (ג) And then you will be blessed, and you will be holy, and you will not be a complete devotee. Let them say after the count:
mishnah-berurah/9:ד: (מב) And when last Yom Tov etc. — therefore specified last Yom Tov for seventh of Pesach does not fall on Motzei Shabbat; on second night of Pesach one does not sanctify in synagogue as siman 487 [Gra and Chayei Adam]
mishnah-berurah/9:ה: (מג) One should count before — as above to exclude we defer day like other matters as much as possible; although here he accepts Yom Tov sanctity in his kiddush nevertheless Shabbat sanctity is greater than Yom Tov sanctity; Taz's view not specifically when last Yom Tov on Motzei Shabbat — likewise even on weekday one should precede counting to kiddush for better to defer sanctity of seventh day from Torah than accept last Yom Tov sanctity which is only d'rabbanan; but Acharonim disagreed
mishnah-berurah/10:א: (מד) Forbidden to eat new grain — meaning grain rooted after 16 Nisan which is time of offering omer; if rooted before omer the omer permits as in Yoreh De'ah 293 — see there; further new grain applies only to five species wheat barley oats rye spelt
mishnah-berurah/10:ב: (מה) Even in our time — as written "and bread and parched grain and groats you shall not eat until this very day" etc. "in all your dwellings" — implies even outside land prohibition applies until essence of day which is day of offering sacrifice 16 Nisan; because of uncertainty of day we are further stringent one more day; in Yoreh De'ah 293 Rama wrote permission for new grain — double doubt: perhaps grain is from previous year; and if this year perhaps rooted before omer; likewise if place bringing grain from places whose grain rooted before omer; Acharonim wrote in Poland one should not be lenient except wheat and rye for majority certainly sown in Cheshvan and new grain does not apply [unless those known sown in summer]; but barley oats spelt majority and almost all sown after Pesach; also not customary to bring grain there from other countries — do not be lenient in them; nevertheless majority of world not careful at all on new grain prohibition; some found merit because difficult to be careful — therefore rely in pressing circumstance on some Rishonim who hold new in chutz la-aretz only d'rabbanan because Sages decreed due to Eretz Yisrael and did not decree except places adjacent to Eretz Yisrael like Egypt and Bavel; some found merit holding new applies only to Israelite grain not gentiles' — therefore must warn Israelites who have grain sown in their fields to observe new grain prohibition; although we cannot protest lenient ones — nevertheless every person of spirit should not rely on these permissions and be stringent for himself in all possible; know further although Acharonim wrote regarding wheat no concern at all perhaps new since majority certainly sown in Cheshvon as today common to bring via railroad wheat flour from distant places; known in inner Russia many places sown in summer and there new grain is found almost more than old — if one knows flour comes from there must be careful in winter months when flour made from new grain; regarding beer and other new grain laws see Yoreh De'ah 293 and Acharonim there
mishnah-berurah/10:ג: (ג) Between Kelly and the Nuclears of the Five Species in Light:
mishnah-berurah/10:ד: (ד) From Carmel, we were not in the hand and not in the light:
mishnah-berurah/10:ה: (ה) (h) Until you get sick and so on, and the last of them, Duff is not careful in the emission of tools if it is not clear that cooking a new formula and it seems that it should not be made worse only in above the first cooking:
mishnah-berurah/10:ו: (ו) (מט) And in Eretz Yisrael until beginning etc. — for there it is only one day, and that we are stringent all day 16 because it is written "until the bone of this day" and we hold "ad" and "ad" include.
turei-zahav/1:א: (א) They begin to count. Even though regarding yovel it is also written "you shall count for yourself," and likewise regarding zavah "she shall count" — the Rabbis learned that this "you shall count" regarding the omer is an actual count, unlike other countings — so Ran.
turei-zahav/1:ב: (ב) And mitzvah for each one. For it is written "you shall count for yourselves" — the count must be for each one. Standing — for the sages taught: "when grain rises you shall begin to count" — do not read "when grain rises" but "when you rise."
turei-zahav/1:ג: (ג) Today one day in the Omer. Such is our custom; but in Ran end of Pesachim that Beit Yosef cites, he mentions "la'omer" with lamed, and our custom appears more correct, for on day one counted at the beginning of night 16 it means days of the omer that will be brought tomorrow on day 16; on later days too "days of the omer" fits all, unlike "la'omer" on night 16 which would mean what was already brought, while "ba'omer" refers only to days of the omer — one cannot explain it on the future offering, for the bet implies within; with lamed one could explain the future offering. One should not say only "today" without "day."
turei-zahav/1:ד: (ד) One week. And not "one" in feminine, as Rashi explained regarding "a full week" — "week" is masculine language.
turei-zahav/2:_: Until stars. Ran wrote counting now is only rabbinic since there is no offering; nevertheless good to count on day one in safeik of darkness so the seven weeks be fully complete — but it is not correct to enter safeik l'chatchila; and if for completeness, in our time any counting at night is called complete.
turei-zahav/3:_: Counts with them without berachah. Meaning his intent is not to fulfill thereby until he blesses at night at home, as Rama wrote — and I do not know what benefit he has counting with the congregation; for Abudraham it fits that he says at the outset: if I remember at night I will return and bless properly, so he did not bless in vain, and if he forgets he already counted; but Rambam himself wrote if he counted without blessing he fulfilled, and that is primary — so this condition is incorrect, for one cannot stipulate a condition contingent on remembering initially, for one does not count a mitzvah from safeik. Why count with the congregation at all? It appears so they not suspect he refuses to count; why does the congregation count while still day — are they wicked? It appears not precise "while still day" but in safeik of darkness as written shortly, and he intends to return and bless at night.
turei-zahav/4:_: If he tells him today such-and-such. It appears simple: if a friend asks how many days of sefirah and he answers "such-and-such days" without mentioning "today such-and-such," he certainly did not fulfill, for the essence of the mitzvah is saying "today such-and-such"; therefore this deals specifically with saying "today such-and-such." Why not answer "today such-and-such" — it is only a reply to one who asks, unlike stam counting that Beit Yosef in Rambam's name says fulfills without intent, except when intent is not to fulfill as Rama wrote shortly — not so, for we find in siman 484 Tur in Rosh's name: if they do not know to bless he reads word by word — proven there he did not fulfill; Rif there: if he wishes he does the whole seder elsewhere first — Rosh relies on this; further proof from siman 658: on first day do not give lulav to a minor before he fulfills — implies on other days permitted, yet when giving to minor he reads berachah word by word and the minor fulfills afterward — unless like intent not to fulfill; so too one answering a questioner — therefore here he warns l'chatchila to avoid this when possible; but if he happened to answer the count of this day without "today" he did not fulfill and must return to count with berachah; therefore better not to tell the count of this day, only "yesterday was such-and-such."
turei-zahav/5:_: And concluded like him — fulfilled. Implies b'dieved; l'chatchila he should not bless until he has clarity at time of berachah how many to count afterward, as above.
turei-zahav/6:_: Opened and said, etc. Tur wrote these distinctions in Abba Eli'ezer's name as a way of safeik; since there is safeik there is safeik for us; Abba Eli'ezer is stringent to bless again since counting is d'oraisa and brings proof from "emet veyatziv" for those who hold it d'oraisa — question: there he did not say emet veyatziv for d'oraisa; but here even if counting d'oraisa, berachot are not me'akev — unless since counting d'oraisa the berachah is also d'oraisa, proven there otherwise why return to bless if berachot are not me'akev. Beit Yosef: from Ran and most poskim counting today is rabbinic — we are lenient; therefore ruled here no second berachah; what is written "and concluded with four" means he counted four, not that he only blessed — questions on both divisions; first: he concluded properly and did not bless at all and counted — fulfilled, berachot not me'akev; Levush challenged this division. Second: concluded improperly — obvious for Abba Eli'ezer he did not fulfill, all the more Shulchan Aruch ruled fulfilled — Maharshal challenged. It appears they were not precise in plain meaning: Abba Eli'ezer and Shulchan Aruch "concluded with five" and second case "concluded four" refer to conclusion of the berachah, not having counted yet — dissonance in berachah words; safeik whether mistaken at start of "Baruch Atah..." or at end — safeik whether berachah is berachah b'dieved and he counts again without berachah, or berachah void as if never blessed and must bless again — like opening intent for wine and concluding for beer — Beit Yosef and Shulchan Aruch ruled for us (counting rabbinic) no second berachah. When intent to conclude as he hears from friend and concluded like him — conclusion is actual counting, berachah was proper at opening and closing and safeik is the counting conclusion; unlike beginning where safeik is in berachah itself and conclusion is in berachah — appears clear if entire berachah was mistaken but he remembered at time of proper counting he must bless again on what he will count — proof from teruma in gemara Tur and Shulchan Aruch siman 206: blessed on fruit, it fell — must bless again on what he will eat though before him, since intent was only for that he blessed on; so one who blessed on Torah shown wrong place must return — siman 140; not applicable here — safeik is in berachah itself like opening for wine ending for beer — not like teruma.
turei-zahav/9:_: After kiddush. Entry of Shabbat pleases us more; what is written "better afterward" is only on last Yom Tov of Passover on Motzei Shabbat when kiddush and havdalah combine — count before kiddush. It appears on the night between seventh day of Passover and eighth day of Passover, even on chol hamoed, one counts before kiddush of last Yom Tov, for better to draw sanctity of seventh day of Passover which is Torah, and last Yom Tov is only rabbinic. Appears simple: one who erred in the day's count and was not known until the next day — like one who forgot entirely; but if he erred in days but not weeks, the weeks still help and afterward he counts days in his manner.
turei-zahav/10:_: Forbidden to eat, etc. Laws of chadash and its permission in our time — see Avi Ezri siman 294 there's help — in ch"l. Beit Yosef siman 481 in Agur's name: meticulous in Israel custom on second Passover night as one festival for everything; one who wishes to eat and drink on second night after Hallel — nothing on him, but not proper to remove himself from meticulous and transgress sages' words.
